name: Baltimore
summary: A port city of rowhouse neighbourhoods on the Chesapeake Bay, known for its harbour, Johns Hopkins, steamed crabs and a strong local arts scene.

curated-2026-10.title: Baltimore places and neighbourhoods written for Prospero Companion
curated-2026-10.note: Well-known public places, institutions and employers from general knowledge. Businesses open and close and rents move: treat this as a snapshot for fiction. Rents are rounded estimates of typical asking ranges, not listings. Coordinates are approximate neighbourhood centres.

curated-climate-2026-10.title: Approximate monthly climate for Baltimore (BWI area)
curated-climate-2026-10.note: Rounded values in line with NOAA 1991-2020 normals; refresh with scripts/world when network access to NOAA is available.

neighborhoods.name: Inner Harbor
neighborhoods.summary: The tourist waterfront: promenade, aquarium, science centre and harbour views, busy on summer weekends.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown
neighborhoods.summary: Office towers, the stadiums, Lexington Market and the theatre district.

neighborhoods.name: Fells Point
neighborhoods.summary: Cobblestone streets, eighteenth-century rowhouses, pubs and live music on the waterfront.

neighborhoods.name: Harbor East
neighborhoods.summary: Polished new towers, hotels, offices and upscale restaurants between downtown and Fells Point.

neighborhoods.name: Little Italy
neighborhoods.summary: A few compact blocks of Italian restaurants, bakeries and bocce, with an outdoor film festival in summer.

neighborhoods.name: Canton
neighborhoods.summary: Former cannery rowhouses turned young-professional hub around O'Donnell Square, with a waterfront park and the marine terminals beyond.

neighborhoods.name: Highlandtown
neighborhoods.summary: Working-class rowhouses beside Patterson Park, with Latin American groceries and an arts district.

neighborhoods.name: Federal Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Hilltop park views over the harbour, a lively bar strip and Cross Street Market.

neighborhoods.name: Locust Point
neighborhoods.summary: A quiet peninsula of rowhouses on the way to Fort McHenry, beside the Domino Sugars plant and its neon sign.

neighborhoods.name: Baltimore Peninsula
neighborhoods.summary: A new mixed-use waterfront district in Port Covington, home to Under Armour's headquarters.

neighborhoods.name: Mount Vernon
neighborhoods.summary: Grand nineteenth-century townhouses around the original Washington Monument, with museums, the Peabody and a strong LGBTQ+ community.

neighborhoods.name: Bolton Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Leafy brick townhouse blocks next to the MICA campus.

neighborhoods.name: Station North
neighborhoods.summary: The arts and entertainment district around Penn Station: murals, studios, an indie cinema and late-night bars.

neighborhoods.name: Remington
neighborhoods.summary: Small rowhouse blocks between Hampden and Charles Village with a food hall and music venues.

neighborhoods.name: Charles Village
neighborhoods.summary: Painted Ladies rowhouses around the Johns Hopkins Homewood campus and the Baltimore Museum of Art.

neighborhoods.name: Hampden
neighborhoods.summary: Former mill village turned quirky shopping strip on 36th Street ("The Avenue"), with thrift shops, cafes and a famous Christmas light block.

neighborhoods.name: Reservoir Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Large Victorian homes on the edge of Druid Hill Park and the Maryland Zoo.

neighborhoods.name: Roland Park
neighborhoods.summary: One of the first planned suburbs in the country: winding streets, large houses, private schools and old trees.

neighborhoods.name: Lauraville
neighborhoods.summary: Northeast Baltimore single-family homes with porches near Morgan State and the Harford Road restaurant strip.

neighborhoods.name: Towson
neighborhoods.summary: The Baltimore County seat just north of the city: Towson University, a large mall, hospitals and a busy suburban downtown.

neighborhoods.name: East Baltimore Midway
neighborhoods.summary: The neighbourhood around the Johns Hopkins medical campus, with new graduate housing beside older rowhouse blocks.

transit.name: Light RailLink
transit.summary: North-south light rail from Hunt Valley through downtown and past the stadiums to BWI Airport.

transit.name: Metro SubwayLink
transit.summary: A single line from Owings Mills through downtown to Johns Hopkins Hospital.

transit.name: CityLink and LocalLink buses
transit.summary: The MTA bus network, the main way around for people without cars.

transit.name: Charm City Circulator
transit.summary: Free downtown buses linking the harbour, Fells Point, Federal Hill, Mount Vernon and Penn Station.

transit.name: Baltimore Water Taxi
transit.summary: Harbour boats between the Inner Harbor, Fells Point, Canton, Harbor East, Locust Point and Fort McHenry.

transit.name: MARC Penn Line
transit.summary: Commuter trains from Penn Station to Washington, D.C., used by many federal workers.

places.name: National Aquarium
places.summary: Big aquarium on the pier with a rooftop rainforest, a coral reef tank and a shark ring.

places.name: Inner Harbor promenade
places.summary: Brick waterfront walk past historic ships, paddle boats and street performers.

places.name: Maryland Science Center
places.summary: Hands-on science museum with a planetarium and IMAX.

places.name: USS Constellation
places.summary: A Civil War-era sloop of war you can board in the harbour.

places.name: Inner Harbor paddle boats
places.summary: Dragon-shaped pedal boats for a slow loop of the harbour.

places.name: Oriole Park at Camden Yards
places.summary: The Orioles' retro ballpark beside the old B&O warehouse.

places.name: M&T Bank Stadium
places.summary: Home of the Ravens; tailgates fill the lots on game days.

places.name: Lexington Market
places.summary: One of the oldest public markets in the country, rebuilt with food stalls including Faidley's crab cakes.

places.name: Hippodrome Theatre
places.summary: Restored 1914 theatre hosting touring Broadway shows.

places.name: Bromo Seltzer Arts Tower
places.summary: Clock tower with artist studios and occasional open-studio days.

places.name: Power Plant Live!
places.summary: An entertainment block of clubs and bars with outdoor concerts in summer.

places.name: Baltimore Farmers' Market & Bazaar
places.summary: Sunday morning market under the Jones Falls Expressway.

places.name: Attman's Delicatessen
places.summary: Century-old deli on Lombard Street's "Corned Beef Row".

places.name: Thames Street waterfront
places.summary: Cobblestones, tug boats and the old Recreation Pier on the harbour edge.

places.name: Broadway Market
places.summary: Historic market hall with lunch counters and seafood.

places.name: Thames Street Oyster House
places.summary: Busy seafood house known for its oyster bar and lobster rolls.

places.name: Blue Moon Cafe
places.summary: Tiny breakfast spot with a weekend line out the door for Cap'n Crunch French toast.

places.name: Bertha's Mussels
places.summary: Old pub with "Eat Bertha's Mussels" bumper-sticker fame and live music.

places.name: The Horse You Came In On Saloon
places.summary: Claims to be one of the oldest continually operating saloons in the country.

places.name: Vaccaro's Italian Pastry Shop
places.summary: Cannoli and gelato institution.

places.name: Sabatino's
places.summary: Old-school red-sauce Italian open late, famous for its "Bookmaker" salad.

places.name: Canton Waterfront Park
places.summary: Small harbour-side park with a water taxi landing and views of the Domino Sugars sign.

places.name: O'Donnell Square
places.summary: A square ringed by bars and restaurants, crowded on weekend nights.

places.name: Captain James Crab House
places.summary: Steamed crabs on butcher paper beside a building shaped like a ship.

places.name: Patterson Park
places.summary: A big city park with a pagoda, a boat lake, an ice rink and weekend soccer.

places.name: Federal Hill Park
places.summary: A steep hilltop with the best free view of the harbour skyline.

places.name: Cross Street Market
places.summary: Renovated market hall with food stalls and a lively after-work crowd.

places.name: American Visionary Art Museum
places.summary: Museum of self-taught "outsider" art, with a mirrored mosaic facade.

places.name: Fort McHenry
places.summary: Star-shaped fort whose 1814 defence inspired "The Star-Spangled Banner", with a shoreline walking path.

places.name: L.P. Steamers
places.summary: Neighbourhood crab house with a rooftop deck.

places.name: Walters Art Museum
places.summary: Free museum with armour, manuscripts and art spanning five thousand years.

places.name: Mount Vernon Place and the Washington Monument
places.summary: The first monument to George Washington, set in four landscaped squares; climbable for a small fee.

places.name: Enoch Pratt Free Library Central Library
places.summary: The grand central library on Cathedral Street.

places.name: Joseph Meyerhoff Symphony Hall
places.summary: Home of the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra.

places.name: Mount Vernon Marketplace
places.summary: Casual food hall with ramen, tacos, oysters and a bar.

places.name: The Charles Theatre
places.summary: Independent cinema showing art films and revival screenings.

places.name: Ottobar
places.summary: Long-running punk and indie rock club.

places.name: R. House
places.summary: Food hall in a former auto body shop with a big patio.

places.name: Baltimore Museum of Art
places.summary: Free art museum with a major Matisse collection and a sculpture garden.

places.name: The Avenue on 36th Street
places.summary: Thrift shops, boutiques, cafes and kitsch along Hampden's main street.

places.name: The Charmery
places.summary: Small-batch ice cream shop with local flavours like Old Bay caramel.

places.name: Ekiben
places.summary: Local favourite for steamed-bun sandwiches and tempura broccoli.

places.name: Jones Falls Trail
places.summary: Paved trail along the stream from the mills to Druid Hill Park and downtown.

places.name: Druid Hill Park
places.summary: Huge park with a reservoir loop, a Victorian conservatory and the Maryland Zoo.

places.name: The Maryland Zoo
places.summary: Zoo in Druid Hill Park known for its African penguin colony.

places.name: Koco's Pub
places.summary: Neighbourhood pub famous for huge crab cakes.

places.name: Towson Town Center
places.summary: The region's big indoor mall.

employers.name: The Johns Hopkins Hospital
employers.summary: The flagship teaching hospital and the city's largest employer group.

employers.name: Johns Hopkins University (Homewood)
employers.summary: Faculty, research and staff jobs on the main campus.

employers.name: University of Maryland Medical Center
employers.summary: Academic hospital with the Shock Trauma Center.

employers.name: Kennedy Krieger Institute
employers.summary: Care and research for children with developmental disabilities.

employers.name: T. Rowe Price
employers.summary: Investment management firm headquartered on the waterfront at Harbor Point.

employers.name: Constellation Energy
employers.summary: Energy company with a headquarters tower in Harbor East.

employers.name: Under Armour
employers.summary: Sportswear company headquartered on the Baltimore Peninsula.

employers.name: Port of Baltimore marine terminals
employers.summary: Container and roll-on/roll-off terminals that employ longshore workers, logisticians and truckers.

employers.name: Baltimore City Public Schools
employers.summary: The city school district, headquartered on North Avenue.

employers.name: Baltimore City government
employers.summary: City agencies around City Hall and the municipal buildings.

employers.name: Baltimore Center Stage
employers.summary: Maryland's state theatre, in a converted school building on North Calvert Street.

career_hubs.name: Hospital and research campuses
career_hubs.summary: Johns Hopkins in East Baltimore and the University of Maryland campus downtown anchor the city's "eds and meds" economy.

career_hubs.name: Harbour business district
career_hubs.summary: Banks, law firms, energy and investment companies, plus hotels and convention work.

career_hubs.name: The port
career_hubs.summary: Marine terminals, warehouses and the Domino Sugars refinery.

climate.summary: Humid subtropical: hot, sticky summers with thunderstorms, mild springs and autumns, and cold but changeable winters with occasional snow.

months.note: Coldest month; a few snow days most years.
Changeable; early blossoms late in the month.

annual_events.name: Orioles Opening Day
annual_events.summary: The baseball season starts at Camden Yards and downtown fills with orange.

annual_events.name: Flower Mart
annual_events.summary: Spring festival around the Washington Monument with flowers and lemon sticks.

annual_events.name: Kinetic Sculpture Race
annual_events.summary: Human-powered art vehicles race over land, mud and harbour water, starting at the American Visionary Art Museum.

annual_events.name: Little Italy open-air film festival
annual_events.summary: Friday night films projected onto a wall in Little Italy.

annual_events.name: Artscape
annual_events.summary: A large free outdoor arts festival; its dates have moved between summer and early autumn.

annual_events.name: Ravens football season
annual_events.summary: Purple Fridays and Sunday game days.

annual_events.name: Fells Point Fun Festival
annual_events.summary: Street festival with music stages and food on the cobblestones.

annual_events.name: Christmas Village
annual_events.summary: German-style Christmas market by the harbour.

annual_events.name: Miracle on 34th Street
annual_events.summary: A block of rowhouses covered in over-the-top Christmas lights.
